:::{#exm-cor-odds-multiplier}

#### Odds of death at the second-lowest beetle dose

<!-- no-figure: the example checks one product of two numbers -->

In @exm-logistic-or-beetles,
$\vxs$ is the lowest dose level and $\vx$ is the next one.
The code computes the [estimated](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/estimation.html#def-estimate) [odds](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-odds) of death at both dose levels
from the `beetles` model (@tbl-beetles-model-grouped).
It then multiplies the odds at $\vxs$ by $\expf{\diffvx \cdot \evb}$.

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
# estimated probabilities of death at the two lowest dose levels
beetles_low_doses <- beetles |> dplyr::slice(1:2)
beetles_low_probs <- predict(
  beetles_glm_grouped,
  newdata = beetles_low_doses,
  type = "response"
)
beetles_low_probs <- unname(beetles_low_probs)
# estimated odds of death at those dose levels
beetles_low_odds <- beetles_low_probs / (1 - beetles_low_probs)
# exp of the dose difference times the dose coefficient
beetles_dose_gap <- beetles$dose[2] - beetles$dose[1]
beetles_dose_coef <- coef(beetles_glm_grouped)[["dose"]]
beetles_gap_term <- beetles_dose_gap * beetles_dose_coef
beetles_multiplier <- exp(beetles_gap_term)
beetles_odds_product <- beetles_low_odds[1] * beetles_multiplier
c(
  odds_lowest = beetles_low_odds[1],
  odds_next = beetles_low_odds[2],
  lowest_times_multiplier = beetles_odds_product
)
```

The estimated odds of death are $`r signif(beetles_low_odds[1], 4)`$ at the lowest dose level.
Multiplying them by $`r signif(beetles_multiplier, 4)`$ gives
$`r signif(beetles_low_odds[1], 4)` \times `r signif(beetles_multiplier, 4)` = `r signif(beetles_odds_product, 4)`$.
That product matches the estimated odds at the next dose level,
as @cor-odds-multiplier states.

:::
